title: Review round 1: Native Sieve interpreter (n3vt)
description: Round 1 review of the sieve-native crate and smtp dep-swap
notes:
SEC1 REVIEW COMPLETE: Maintainer risk = MEDIUM. The ~2000-line crate is well-written and maintainable by a solo dev, but has MEDIUM risk in three areas:

1. FANCY-REGEX DRIFT (HIGH): pinned at v0.13.0, latest is v0.18.0. Regex matching behavior could change silently. Glob-to-regex code lacks edge-case tests. Impact: silent matching bugs on upgrade.

2. ORACLE DRIFT (MEDIUM): cross-validation uses sieve-rs as oracle, but if sieve-rs updates, no documented procedure for resolving divergence. Solo maintainer without Sieve expertise cannot reliably verify RFC 5228/5229 correctness.

3. RFC EXPERTISE DEPENDENCY (MEDIUM): inline comments reference RFC sections but don't explain semantic rules (e.g., why 'ignore unknown commands' is fail-safe). Solo maintainer without RFC knowledge will struggle to refactor safely.

ASSESSMENT DETAIL:
- Code quality: GOOD (no unsafe, explicit errors, clean structure)
- Test coverage: ADEQUATE for happy path (28 unit + 13 integration tests, all passing)
- Test gaps: Regex edge cases, address extraction edge cases, variable substitution edge cases
- Cross-validation oracle: VALID but insufficient for spec compliance (independent impl, not reference impl)

4 TASK ISSUES FILED (P2-P3):
- stoa-195c1d21.3: fancy-regex version pinning & upgrade path
- stoa-195c1d21.4: oracle drift mitigation plan  
- stoa-195c1d21.5: parse error location info (low impact)
- stoa-195c1d21.6: RFC documentation for solo maintainers

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Address P2 (fancy-regex, edge-case tests) before next major version
- Add Sieve expertise or external reference tests before heavy refactoring
- Document oracle divergence procedure in CLAUDE.md before deploying to production
